title: Cuba Announces New Migration Law — Diaspora Investor Rights and End to Return Restrictions
detail: Cuba's government announced a sweeping new Migration, Foreigners, and Citizenship Law package that fundamentally reformed the island's relationship with its diaspora. Key provisions eliminated the previous 24-month time limit for Cubans residing abroad — which previously triggered loss of residency rights and property ownership on the island — and established 'Effective Migratory Residence' status for long-term diaspora members. The reform also introduced investor status allowing Cubans living abroad to legally own and invest in private businesses on the island for the first time. The package — enacted amid the deepest economic crisis in Cuba's post-Soviet history — was designed to stimulate remittances and diaspora investment at a moment when fuel shortages and blackouts were devastating the domestic economy. Critics noted the reforms, while significant, stopped far short of the political changes demanded by the US as conditions for lifting the energy blockade.

media.caption: Cuba's new migration law extends rights to diaspora investors
